episode_title: Tipper X Talks: Inside Wall Street's Biggest Sting, From Informing to Redemption

real_qa.q: What is the fraud triangle and how did it lead Tom Harden to commit insider trading?
real_qa.r: The fraud triangle consists of three elements: pressure, opportunity, and rationalization. In Tom's case, his boss moved the monthly profit goal from one to three years to monthly performance targets, creating pressure. He was then given the opportunity to buy stocks under 1% of the fund without oversight. Finally, he rationalized his behavior by telling himself everyone was doing it, that it was just one time, and that he was not hurting anyone. He bought a 0.9% position and made $46,000 personally across four trades, which he now calls the price of his professional career at age 29.
real_qa.requete: fraud triangle insider trading pressure opportunity rationalization

real_qa.q: How much money did Tom Harden personally make from his four insider trades?
real_qa.r: Tom Harden made $46,000 personally from his four insider trades, while the firm made just over a million dollars on these same trades. He describes this $46,000 as the price of his professional career at 29 years old, a number he has to live with for the rest of his life and often mentions in his corporate talks.

real_qa.q: What percentage of major public companies taken private by private equity in 2006 showed unexplained price spikes before deal announcements?
real_qa.r: Sixty percent of the biggest public companies taken private by private equity in 2006 had unexplained price spikes before the deal was announced, a figure that was significantly up from a few years prior. This normalized the kind of insider trading that was occurring and set the tone for what Tom was seeing around him in the hedge fund industry.
real_qa.requete: 60 percent companies private equity 2006 price spikes

real_qa.q: When did the FBI first approach Tom Harden and where was he?
real_qa.r: The FBI first approached Tom Harden on July 8th, 2008, at 6:30 in the morning near 55th and 8th Avenue in New York, close to his apartment, while he was dropping off dry cleaning. Two FBI agents with dark suits and badges approached him and later offered him the opportunity to cooperate as an informant.
real_qa.requete: Tom Harden FBI approached July 8 2008 dry cleaning

real_qa.q: How long did Tom Harden cooperate with the FBI before speaking to a defense attorney?
real_qa.r: Tom Harden cooperated with the FBI for almost two years before he ever spoke to an attorney. When he finally called a defense attorney, the attorney's first question was who his previous attorney was, and upon learning there was none, the attorney told him he should have hired legal representation the first day the FBI approached him.
real_qa.requete: Tom Harden FBI two years no lawyer cooperated

real_qa.q: What are the key warning signs that an organization is creating conditions for misconduct?
real_qa.r: Three patterns indicate an organization is creating conditions for misconduct: a blame culture where people get punished for mistakes and stop surfacing problems; communication breakdown and silos where nobody feels safe raising a hand; and a fear-based culture where people rationalize how to get around problems instead of walking them up the chain. Additional warning signs include running ethics surveys without sharing results, labeling employees who speak up as tiresome, and rewarding behaviors that contradict stated leadership values.
real_qa.requete: organizational warning signs misconduct compliance culture

guest.titre_secondaire: Former Hedge Fund Analyst and FBI Informant (Tipper X)
guest.bio_context: Tom Harden is a hedge fund analyst who, in the mid-2000s, engaged in insider trading while working at a tech-focused hedge fund and subsequently became one of the FBI's most prolific informants, known as Tipper X. He cooperated with the FBI for nearly two years on cases involving major insider trading schemes before his name became public. He is the author of Wired on Wall Street, which recounts his rise, fall, and redemption through his involvement in a major financial crime investigation.
